architectural_fidelity.reason: Same window position and size, same camera angle and viewpoint, same ceiling height, same wall color (light neutral), and same flooring visible on right side

furniture_removal.reason: All original furniture completely removed—no ghost outlines of the black sofa, papasan chair, glass coffee table, or side table visible

style_commitment.reason: This is a generic neutral coastal/minimalist room, not COVABOHEMIAN—lacks bohemian essential markers like rich textiles, eclectic patterns, layered rugs, macrame beyond single wall piece, vibrant colors, global accessories, or maximalist layering

editorial_density.reason: Has wall art (macrame frame), plants (2 visible), textiles (pillows, throw), wicker poufs, but lacks the layered, curated abundance expected at Architectural Digest level—feels understaged and sparse

photorealism.reason: Overall lighting is soft and realistic, but furniture has a slightly washed-out, low-contrast appearance that borders on CGI flatness—material textures lack depth compared to Collov's tactile rendering

designer_preference_reason: Cova failed to deliver the requested bohemian style, producing instead a safe neutral room that lacks the personality and conviction a client paying for 'bohemian' would expect.
what_cova_does_better: Maintains exact architectural fidelity to original room
Clean furniture removal with no artifacts
what_collov_does_better: Superior photorealism with tactile material rendering and dimensional depth
Confident style commitment with clear editorial vision
Richer layering and editorial density appropriate to luxury staging
specific_fixes_if_failing: Add authentic bohemian elements: layered patterned rugs (Persian, Turkish, Moroccan), rich jewel tones (terracotta, mustard, deep teal), textured throws
Include eclectic mix of global accessories, multiple plants in varied vessels, floor cushions, poufs with pattern
Layer wall art with macrame, woven baskets, and framed ethnic prints
Increase contrast and texture definition in rendering—materials should read as fabric, wood, and wicker, not monotone neutrals
Add visual weight and warmth through layered textiles on furniture (multiple throw pillows with varying patterns, draped blankets)
